content:
I’m deeply honoured to share that I recently completed my judicial internship at the High Court of Judicature at Patna, under the esteemed mentorship of Hon’ble Mr. Justice Ashok Kumar Pandey.

Over the past month, I had the privilege of observing the judicial process up close sitting through courtroom proceedings, assisting with legal research, and watching firsthand how statutes, precedents, and constitutional principles come alive in real cases. Each hearing was a reminder that law is not just a body of rules, but a living instrument in the service of justice.

This experience sharpened my legal reasoning and deepened my respect for the discipline and integrity that define judicial work.

My sincere thanks to Hon’ble Mr. Justice Ashok Kumar Pandey, and to everyone who made this such a formative chapter of my journey.

comment: Courtroom exposure often reveals the gap between legal theory and judicial practicality. Learning how judges weigh facts, precedent, and procedure is what shapes sound legal judgment over time.
